observation.visible_scene: A person in a gray/red striped button-up shirt works at a table on a large, glossy black rectangular sheet that mirrors the shirt and the recording device. The right hand grips a green plastic squeegee and presses it onto the sheet; the left hand pinches the top edge of the sheet to hold it flat. Static scenery surrounds the workspace: pink-handled scissors and a curled white paper on the left, a red toad figurine and a brown-and-gold monkey figurine on the right, a rolled pale tube behind, and scattered water droplets on the tabletop. Water droplets also sit on the upper-left of the sheet in the early frames.
visible_changes: The green squeegee is repeatedly stroked across the black surface: it travels from the upper area downward toward the bottom edge (frames ~1-10), is lifted clear of the sheet and brought back up (frames ~11-13), then re-applied and swept down again (frames ~14-24), lifted and moved over the left portion (frames ~25-29), and continues with further back-and-forth strokes concentrated on the left half (frames ~30-41).
The holding left hand stays at the top edge of the sheet throughout, with only small positional adjustments; the sheet itself remains laid flat and is not flipped or removed.

The reflection of the person's torso and the camera shifts across the sheet as the squeegee and hands move, and the distinct droplets on the sheet's surface become less prominent as strokes pass over them.

The framing of the scene drifts slightly (the sheet's top edge and the right-side figurines sit lower/more cropped in later frames), indicating either a small camera tilt or the operator leaning, but the relative layout of objects is preserved.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the black sheet is (film, glass, protective layer) and the goal of the squeegeeing.
Whether the segment is the start, middle, or end of the smoothing task; the strokes are already ongoing at t=0 and continue at the last frame.
Any liquid source, wiping, or trimming that happens outside this crop.
uncertain_details: Whether the slight change in object positions is camera movement or the operator's body shifting; background evidence is limited.
The exact material of the green tool and the sheet.
Whether droplets are being removed or merely spread by the strokes.
